items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: A young man was waiting for me at the airport. He presented himself as Serge Griffin. ... I learned that Serge Griffin was the accountaſnt for the Edouard 7th theatre

ctx.x: But what saved the situation was an announcement that the flight would be delayed an hour because of motor trouble or something. So I grabbed a taxi, went back to the Normans, had the taxi to wait for me, made some quick changes and taken only the things that would be necessary for a few weeks, jumped back in the taxi and made it back down to the Air France office on 5th Avennue in time for the bus going to the Airport. My brother didn't come to the bus terminus because he had been up all night with me while I…

The flight was 15 hours and there was a stop in the Azore Island somewhere for more than an hour early the morning of the 12th which was Sunday. When we arrived over the French coast, it was raining cats and dogs,as the saying goes. Arriving at Orly near Paris, it was pouring down little devils and pitchforks. A young man was waiting for me at the airport. He presented himself as Serge Griffin. I was expecting Charles Delaunay to meet me because we knew each other and it was he that had arranged a contract for me…
The last concert I remember doing in Paris was the 3rd of July, 1936. I left Paris in December 1938 for Egypt, and now it was 10 years later that I was back again.
